chains.title: TFAP2A drives altered IRF6 regulation via allele-specific enhancer binding

links.claim: The alt allele (G) increases TFAP2A binding in QBiC-SELEX models; literature reports that rs642961 abrogates AP2A binding at MCS9.7, consistent with the risk allele A reducing TFAP2A occupancy. ENCODE has no TFAP2A ChIP peak at this exact site, so occupancy is inferred from the literature rather than ENCODE.
The variant is located within an active distal enhancer-like region (dELS) with DNase and H3K27ac enhancer marks.
TFAP2A binding at the MCS9.7 enhancer regulates IRF6, a gene required for oral epithelial development and orofacial cleft risk.
The functional regulatory activity is relevant to oral epithelium, including fetal oral epithelial cells used in enhancer assays.
Reduced TFAP2A binding and altered IRF6 enhancer activity contribute to orofacial cleft risk; rs642961 is associated with orofacial clefts with effect allele A.

predictions: The alt allele G increases TFAP2A binding at the variant site.
The risk allele A reduces TFAP2A occupancy and IRF6 enhancer activity in oral epithelial cells.
falsified_if: TFAP2A does not bind the rs642961-containing enhancer in oral epithelial cells.
The A and G alleles show no TFAP2A-dependent difference in IRF6 enhancer activity.

chains.title: ETV3 modulates IRF6 via increased alt allele binding affinity

links.claim: The alt allele (G) increases ETV3 binding in QBiC-SELEX through a CIS-BP-mapped ETV5 model; ETV3 occupancy at this site is unknown because no ETV3 ChIP peak is shown.
The variant is located within an active distal enhancer-like region (dELS).
The alt allele G is associated with lower IRF6 expression in brain eQTL data; no craniofacial-cell eQTL is provided for ETV3-dependent IRF6 regulation.
The regulatory effect would need to occur in cells relevant to craniofacial development, but no cell-type evidence is provided.

If ETV3 represses IRF6, increased alt-allele ETV3 binding would lower IRF6 and could contribute to cleft lip risk; however, the cleft association in E6 is with allele A, opposite the alt-G binding increase, so this chain is weak.

predictions: The alt allele G increases ETV3 binding at the variant site.
ETV3 occupancy at this element alters IRF6 expression in a craniofacial cell type.
falsified_if: ETV3 does not occupy the rs642961-containing enhancer in relevant cells.
Changing ETV3 binding does not affect IRF6 expression.

predictions: The variant rs642961 influences Cleft lip phenotype through a mechanism unrelated to direct TF binding at this specific enhancer element.
falsified_if: A functional TF-mediated regulatory change is identified at the variant locus affecting IRF6 or other critical downstream genes.

Its expression in the oral epithelium depends on the transcription factor TFAP2A.
The IRF6 enhancer MCS-9.7 is bound and activated by the transcription factor SOX9, mutations of which cause Pierre Robin sequence, a craniofacial anomaly that includes cleft palate.

To identify candidates for functional SNPs at eight such loci we conduct a massively parallel reporter assay in a fetal oral epithelial cell line, revealing SNPs with allele-specific effects on enhancer activity.
Conditional analyses of GWAS data suggest the two functional SNPs near IRF6 account for the majority of risk for CL/P at this locus.
Additionally, a variant in an enhancer (MCS9.7) that regulates IRF6 is associated with risk for isolated orofacial clefting.
This variant (rs642961) abrogates AP2A protein binding at MCS9.7.
TFAP2A rs1675414 was associated with NSCLO, replicated by both case-control and family based tests.
The current investigation suggests an intriguing role of TFAP2A in the etiology of NSCLO among the Vietnamese population.

Analysing the craniofacial TF TFAP2A in human embryonic palatal mesenchyme (HEPM) cells, we identified 2845 TFAP2A ChIP-seq peaks, several of which were located near nsCL/P candidate genes (e.g. MSX1 and SPRY2).
Integration with nsCL/P GWAS data, however, did not show robust evidence for co-localization of common nsCL/P risk variants with TFAP2A ChIP-seq peaks.
Mutations in IRF6, TFAP2A and GRHL3 cause orofacial clefting syndromes in humans.
